meta.separate_fields_note: syllabus_entitlement, exam_emphasis and pedagogical_prerequisites are separate fields in every bullet record; none is derived from another.

assessment_structure.source: ROOT/src/syllabus.txt (pdf pages = printed page + 4); tables checked visually on PDF pages 18 and 19

papers.description: short-answer questions and novel data for interpretation and questions testing enquiry skills; all questions compulsory

sections.description: Longer questions requiring interpretation and analysis of real economic situations
sections.assessed_by: Assessment Objectives B and C (as printed)

papers.description: structured questions for interpretation and analysis of real economic situations; seeks to cover AO A, B, C

sections.description: Structured question(s), compulsory; 'will include drawing and interpretation of diagrams'
Learners answer 3 of 5 structured essay questions at 20 marks each (100 marks set)

assessment_structure.observed_in_papers: All ten papers match: P1 = 40 (Sec A) + 40 (Sec B); P2 = 20 (Q1 compulsory) + five 20-mark optional questions (Q2-Q6), three to be answered. P1 Section B: 2020 had Q23 [23] + Q24 [17]; 2021-2024 are 20 + 20 (2024 has only Q23 and Q24). Set marks per year: P1 80, P2 120.

assessment_objectives.name: Knowledge with understanding
elements: economic phenomena, facts, definitions, concepts, principles and theories

assessment_objectives.name: Application and analysis
elements: use economic data, recognise patterns, deduce relationships
analyse economic knowledge in verbal, numerical, diagrammatic, pictorial and graphical form
recognise that economic theory is subject to limitations and uncertainties

assessment_objectives.name: Evaluation and decision making
elements: distinguish evidence from opinion, make reasoned judgements
evaluate social and environmental implications of courses of economic action
make decisions and suggest proposals based on novel data

specification_grid.note: Percentages are of each paper's 80 marks as printed. P1 A = 50% equals Section A's 40 marks, consistent with the scheme text. No mark scheme exists to check paper-level or question-level AO allocation; none is invented here.

command_words.definition: examine in detail to show meaning, identify elements and the relationship between them
work out from given facts, figures or information
state the points of a topic / give characteristics and main features
write about issue(s) or topic(s) in depth in a structured way
judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something
set out purposes or reasons / make the relationships between things evident / provide why and/or how, and support with relevant evidence
produce an answer from a given source or recall/memory
apply knowledge and understanding to situations where there are a range of valid responses in order to make proposals / put forward considerations

command_word_observations.note: Syllabus table (p18) defines 13 words. Paper stems also use name, list, write down, why, what, how, which, comment, consider, assess, examine, advise, distinguish, use, mention, which are undefined there; 'assess', 'comment', 'compare', 'contrast' appear in the AO text (p13) but 'comment', 'compare', 'contrast' have no table definition. Two stems in the same paper can ask for the same demand with different words (e.g. 2023 P2 'Distinguish' vs 2021 P2 'Describe' fiscal/monetary).

grade_descriptions.note: Descriptors for A, C, E and G only; qualitative, no marks or boundaries.

other_scheme_facts.fact: Guided learning hours about 130 over two years; 8 periods of 40 min per 7-day cycle or 6 per 5-day cycle
Progression to NSSCAS Economics for grades C to A*

internal_tensions: Scheme says P1 Section A is assessed by AO A only (p14), but Section A items in 2020-2024 include calculations (e.g. 2022 Q13, 2024 Q17), reading diagrams (2020 Q8, 2022 Q9-10, 2024 Q9) and 'explain'/'describe' items; the syllabus's own AO text places 'calculate' and 'explain' under B.

Grid A/B/C percentages cannot be reproduced from the papers without a mark scheme; ER-printed labels (Kn/Ap/An/Ev) are partial and sometimes at odds with the syllabus verb bands (e.g. 2024 P1 Q23(a) 'Describe' labelled Application and analysis; 2022 P2 Q4(b) labelled Kn).

Some specific-objective bullets contain no content list ('types of markets', 'aims of trade unions', 'factors affecting trade union activities in Namibia'), so adequate response has to be authored from outside sources.

method: Unit: each question part's printed mark (from the QP .txt, summed per section to confirm 40+40 for every P1 and 20+100 for every P2: all 20 section totals reconciled).

Assignment: every part's full marks go to ONE primary bullet (this audit's judgement; see inferred_not_printed). Secondary tags are recorded but not counted. 5 marks are unmapped (2023 P1 Q25b percentage change 2; 2023 P2 Q1c arithmetic 1; 2024 P2 Q2a 'investment' 2).
Denominators: 'set marks' = all marks printed on the papers = 200 per year (P1 80 + P2 20 + 5 x 20) = 1000 over 2020-2024. 'Compulsory marks' = P1 (80) + P2 Section A (20) = 100 per year = 500.
Topic share = topic marks / 1000 (or / 500 compulsory). Topic marks are summed from the bullet-level assignments.
No AO allocation and no marking guidance have been computed or invented; AO labels are quoted only where printed in the reports.
